name: UI Microstudy
tagline: One crisp interface component morphs into the next while a cursor clicks, drags and hovers, and the colour field changes every beat.
description: A code-made UI motion study for product tours, feature reels and design-engineering showcases. A single white or near-black pill or card sits dead centre on a flat saturated colour with a few faint circles and bands. A cursor performs a real interaction, the card springs into its next shape, and a circular wipe swaps the background colour on every beat. The preview morphs through ten components, from a button and music player to a stat card, command palette and toast stack.

display.usage: All UI text. Headline numbers 108px/800 with -0.045em tracking, labels 24–32px/600, captions 18–22px/500; tabular numerals

body.usage: Secondary labels and sublines in muted grey (#8d8d9a on dark, #6b6b76 on white)

mono.usage: Tiny technical captions (shortcut hints, the wordmark subline) at 20–22px

transitions: card morph: width, height and border-radius spring to the next component's size with back.out(1.5) in ~0.6s
circular wipe from the frame centre (clip-path circle 0 to 1180px, 0.7s) reveals the next background colour
old content fades and shrinks to 0.94 in 0.14s, new content fades up 0.16s into the morph
textAnimations: number tick to the new value over 0.9s with power3.out
typed query: letters appear on 0.06s beats with a moving orange caret
emoji, stars and chart dots pop in with scale 0 to 1, back.out(2.6–3)
wordmark letters rise 60px with back.out(2) and 0.03s stagger

rhythm.notes: Ten morphs in 8s: about 0.65–0.9s per component, 1.15s for the stat card. Each beat is one cursor action (hover, press, drag) then a morph. Close with a small dark confirmation pill that reads 'every frame is code', then a wordmark card on the opening colour.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- Put exactly one element on screen, centred on a flat saturated field (#ff5c93, #7c4dff, #0fb5a6, #2f5bff, #ff7a1a, #1fc76a, #ffc82e, #ff4a2b). Add 3 faint shapes (a 10% white disc, a 24% white ring, a 5% black diagonal band); never gradients or glows.
- Cards are white (#ffffff) or ink (#17171d), 88–104px tall pills (radius = height/2) or 300–420px cards (radius 34–44), with a two-layer soft shadow (0 34px 70px -14px rgba(20,10,40,.36) + 0 10px 22px rgba(20,10,40,.16)). Keep them 340–760px wide on a 1920 frame.
- Use one persistent card element and tween width/height/border-radius with back.out(1.5) over ~0.6s into the next shape; old content fades and shrinks to 0.94 in 0.14s, new content fades up 0.16s into the morph. Change the background colour on every morph with a centre-out circular clip-path wipe (power3.out, 0.7s), never reusing a neighbouring colour.
- A black arrow cursor with a white outline drives every beat: arrive with power3.out, scale to 0.8 and spring back (back.out(3)) on press, drag with power2.inOut while the thing it drags uses the same tween so they never drift apart.
- Animate the content, not just the shell: tick numbers (power3.out), draw lines with pathLength dashoffset, type text on 0.06s beats with a moving orange caret, pop small icons at scale 0 to 1 with back.out(2.6–3). Draw icons as inline SVG, never system emoji.
- Typography is Inter only: 600–800 weights, tight tracking (-0.01em body, -0.045em on big 108px numbers), tabular numerals, muted #8d8d9a / #6b6b76 sublines, JetBrains Mono 20–22px for tiny technical captions. Copy is specific and short.
- Rhythm: about 0.65–1.2s per beat, each beat one cursor action (hover, press, drag) then a morph. Avoid centred titles, drop-in text blocks, or anything holding longer than 1.3s without a cursor action.
- Optional motif: end on a small dark confirmation pill carrying the tagline, then a wordmark card on the opening colour with letters rising 60px (back.out(2), 0.03s stagger).
example: The preview morphs one card through ten interface components (a button, music player, volume bar, stat card with a ticking number, command palette, star rating, toast stack) while a cursor clicks and drags, ending on a 'frame' wordmark. Don't copy this scene unless asked.
